requirements.text: Individual validation reports are shared with the ECB no later than one month after they are finalised and approved by management.
requirements.level_reason: Supervisory submission obligation of the institution; evidenced in the transmission records to the ECB, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: The validation tools are applied separately to each rating system approved at the start of the observation period, covering all customers or facilities within its range of application.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Validation tool results are submitted to the ECB in the ECB templates together with the annual internal validation report, at consolidated level unless the Decision states otherwise.
requirements.level_reason: Supervisory reporting obligation of the institution; evidenced in the annual submission of the ECB templates, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: The validation tools use the one-year observation period of the internal validation, with the annual end date kept constant across reporting years.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Templates are named [LEICode]_[ModelType]_[ModelID]_[ReferenceDate]_[VersionNumber], with the reference date as the end of the observation period (DDMMYYYY).
requirements.level_reason: Formal requirement on supervisory submission files; evidenced in the reporting submission to the ECB, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: The validation function's overall assessment is reported on the four-point scale; major deficiencies indicate a potential RWEA impact of at least ±5% and severe deficiencies at least ±10%.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Portfolio information (RWEA, EAD, number of customers or facilities, number of grades, number of defaults) is reported for the beginning and end of the observation period.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Rating process statistics report customers with outdated ratings or financial statements, transferred ratings and process-deficiency exclusions relative to portfolio size M, with their PDs and defaults.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: The relative frequency of customers with overrides in the validation sample (M_def/N) is reported at portfolio level.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: PD calibration is tested with a one-sided Jeffreys test at portfolio and rating-grade level, reporting the Beta(D+1/2, N−D+1/2) distribution function evaluated at the PD as p-value.
requirements.quote: the PD applied in the portfolio/rating grade at the beginning of the relevant observation period is greater than the true one
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Discriminatory power is tested by comparing the current AUC with the AUC at initial validation/development, using S = (AUCinit − AUCcurr)/s and p-value 1 − Φ(S).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Customer migrations over the observation period are summarised with the upper and lower matrix weighted bandwidth (MWB) statistics at portfolio level.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Stability of the migration matrix is assessed with pairwise z-tests on the monotonicity of off-diagonal transition frequencies for each rating grade.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Concentration in rating grades is assessed with the Herfindahl index, testing the current coefficient of variation against that at initial validation (number-weighted; exposure-weighted HI also reported).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: LGD is back-tested with a one-sided paired t-test of realised versus estimated LGD on facilities whose recovery closed in the observation period, at portfolio and grade/pool (or 12-segment) level.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to own LGD estimates only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: LGD discriminatory power is tested by comparing the current generalised AUC (gAUC) with the gAUC at initial validation/development.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to own LGD estimates only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: ELBE is back-tested against realised LGD with a two-sided paired t-test at portfolio and grade/pool or segment level, at various reference points in default.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to own LGD estimates only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: CCF estimates are back-tested with a one-sided paired t-test of realised versus estimated CCF at facility grade or pool level, excluding facilities covered by an EAD approach.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to own estimates of conversion factors only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).
